subcategory: citation attribution via a retrieval-augmented validation agent
task: Citation attribution for scientific text (find the reference a human author would cite)
problem: LLM-as-a-judge is unreliable for citation evaluation: GPT-4o recognises wrong citations but rejects correct ones, with recall as low as 16-17% when judging from abstracts.
architecture: CiteGuard: an LLM agent extending CiteAgent with retrieval actions over Semantic Scholar - search by citation count and relevance, read/find_in_text, ask_for_more_context (fetch surrounding sentences of the excerpt) and search_text_snippet (search inside paper full texts); iterative runs exclude already selected papers to suggest alternative valid citations.
retriever: Semantic Scholar API search actions (title/abstract relevance, citation count, full-text snippet search)
generator: GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, Kimi-K2, Qwen3, Gemini 2.0 Flash
knowledge_source: Semantic Scholar paper metadata and full-text snippets
llm_or_encoder: GPT-4o / DeepSeek-R1 / Kimi-K2 / Qwen3 / Gemini 2.0 Flash

datasets.name: CiteME
datasets.details: 130 excerpts from computer-science papers, each with one missing citation

datasets.name: CiteMulti
datasets.details: 10 multi-citation CS paragraphs plus 20 biomedical and 20 physics/math excerpts

key_results: With GPT-4o, accuracy 45.1% vs 35.4% for CiteAgent on CiteME (5-run averages).
With DeepSeek-R1, CiteGuard reaches 68.1% accuracy, close to human performance of 69.2%.
Replacing snippet search by reading the full paper raises accuracy by 3.07% at about 2x the tokens.
strengths: Reframes citation evaluation as attribution alignment with human authors; ablates each new retrieval action.
Model-agnostic across proprietary/open and reasoning/non-reasoning LLMs; human evaluation of alternative citations.

limitations.text: Performance is bounded by the coverage and retrieval quality of the Semantic Scholar API.
Not tested with small open models (<1B parameters).
Gains on the cross-domain CiteMulti set are smaller than on CiteME, attributed to domain shift and citation styles.

notes: Benchmark is small (130 excerpts); results averaged over 5 runs.
title: CiteGuard: Faithful Citation Attribution for LLMs via Retrieval-Augmented Validation
